title: Grateful Dead Live at Civic Auditorium on 1969-01-17
lineage: CD -> Samplitude Professional v10.02 -> Cool Edit Pro v2.0 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording of the January 17 1969 show is clean and crisp, capturing a stellar early‑'69 set highlighted by a soaring Dark Star and superb The Eleven.
ai_review.review: This Charlie Miller soundboard capture presents a vivid snapshot of the Dead’s breakthrough year – Jerry’s guitar is described as “god‑like,” the band locks into an expansive Dark Star, and The Eleven shines with tight yet free interplay. The mix is clear with a slightly forward bass drum, and the tape has been pitch‑corrected to restore the original tempo, though a few listeners note Lovelight feels a touch slow and Cosmic Charlie runs ragged.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews are 5‑star, praising the performance and noting only minor recording quirks; the show is consistently called one of the best early‑'69 dates, yielding a high combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean mix with crisp snare and clear vocals; bass drum is prominent (Mickey Hart) but not objectionable. Tape has been pitch‑corrected to A=440, fixing earlier speed issues. No major dropouts or distortion reported.

poor_songs: Turn On Your Love Light (tempo feels a tad slow)
Cosmic Charlie (described as messy by some)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑'69 set builds from the fresh, exploratory Dark Star into tight group improvisations on The Eleven and St Stephen, with high energy peaks in Death Don't Have No Mercy and a wild ending on Cosmic Charlie; overall pacing is praised despite the slightly slower Lovelight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly called “god‑like” with phenomenal tone and phrasing; his playing on Dark Star is highlighted as a major leap forward.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass work noted as prominent and enjoyable; his fingerprints are especially evident on Cosmic Charlie and the bass riffs throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocal lines quoted (“They say that is all there is…”); no specific criticism, generally supportive of his rhythm guitar and vocals.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten (TC) present but not prominent; reviewers feel his keyboards are “over‑thought” and still finding a voice in this era.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s bass drum sits high in the mix; snare drums are crisp and well captured, with no major issues noted.
